basis: Definition specifies Kunjin viral infection of the brain causing encephalitis.
Congenital absence of skin; autosomal recessive inheritance does not establish additional organ involvement.
Isolated congenital accessory auricular tag, an external-ear developmental anomaly; no additional organ disease specified.
Segmental infantile hemangioma is a cutaneous vascular tumor; isolated disease does not imply associated brain, cardiac or other malformations.
Immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation of skin; systemic sarcoidosis is not required by this cutaneous concept.
Malignant mixed epithelial-stromal tumor originates in the kidney.
Severe developmental delay and epilepsy define disease; laryngomalacia directly affects the airway in 26/35 patients (~74%).
Clear-cell morphologic variant of basal cell carcinoma arising in skin.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; hypoplastic nails and sparse postpubertal hair are described as typical, supporting common (>30%) ectodermal involvement.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability commonly define this deletion umbrella; additional malformations vary with the deleted region.
Benign squamous epithelial tumor of skin; an infectious cause is not established by this concept.
Platelet dense-body deficiency and oculocutaneous albinism define disease; restrictive lung dysfunction occurs in 3/7 (~43%), although fibrosis is reported in 1/7.
Disease is explicitly located in the parasympathetic nervous system; downstream organ damage is not specified.
Neoplasm originates in buccal oral mucosa, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Megalencephaly is an obligate structural brain abnormality; other reported findings do not establish additional organ involvement.
Occlusion directly affects a retinal vein, involving both the eye and its venous vasculature.
Sorbitol dehydrogenase deficiency is an inborn metabolic disorder causing peripheral motor-sensory neuropathy; weakness reflects denervation.
Carcinoma originates in mammary ducts of the nipple; breast has no axis.
Filariae occupy skin/subcutis and cause chronic skin disease; damaging ocular involvement is variable and not established in >=30% across all infections.
Central hypoventilation defines respiratory/autonomic dysfunction; achalasia and intestinal/esophageal dysmotility occur in 3/3. Direct causation of isolated eye/spine findings is unclear.
Inflammation of hair follicles; this umbrella includes infectious and sterile causes and does not establish a specific infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Ulceration is confined to vulva/lower vagina; associated infections alone do not establish direct infection or a definite immune-mediated mechanism.
Eyelid, lip and dental malformations define disease; sparse hair occurs in 7/8 (~88%) and nail dysplasia in 5/8 (~63%). Neural tube defects occur in only 2/8.
Bilateral duplication of the biphalangeal thumb is a congenital skeletal malformation.
Structural/functional incompetence affects the soft palate and pharyngeal closure; hearing impairment is frequent (30-79%).
